title: Forecast Monitoring & Retraining
interviewAnswer: Forecast systems need monitoring for bias, scale changes, missing updates, driver drift and horizon-specific error. Retraining cadence should reflect how quickly relationships change and whether new labels arrive.
keyPoints: Bias can matter more than symmetric error.
why: Forecast Monitoring & Retraining appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Forecast systems need monitoring for bias, scale changes, missing updates, driver drift and horizon-specific error. Retraining cadence should reflect how quickly relationships change and whether new labels arrive. Bias can matter more than symmetric error. Backfill/revisions complicate evaluation. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A demand forecast can have acceptable MAE overall but persistent underforecast bias for high-value SKUs.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Forecast Monitoring & Retraining make?
How would you validate or debug Forecast Monitoring & Retraining in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
